name: Bhutan
snapshot: The Himalayan kingdom of Gross National Happiness, now trying to stem an exodus of young people with a new mindfulness city on the Indian border.
culture: Bhutan protects its Buddhist culture deliberately: national dress is required in offices, buildings follow traditional design, and tsechu festivals feature masked cham dances. Archery is the national sport. Dzongs, fortress-monasteries, serve as both religious and administrative centres. Television and the internet only arrived in 1999.
society: Bhutan measures progress by Gross National Happiness and is one of the few carbon-negative countries, with most land under forest. Hydropower sold to India is the main export. A high-value, low-volume tourism policy charges visitors a daily fee. Many young Bhutanese have left for Australia, prompting the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.
baseline: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has reigned since 2006, after his father introduced democracy from above. Tshering Tobgay's People's Democratic Party won the 2024 election.

leaders.state: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, since 2006
